entry.title: Dynamic v3.1 GGUFs + Performance Fixes
entry.content:
Qwen3.8-27B is here with Dynamic v3.1 GGUFs, ready to run locally with Unsloth. This release also brings major performance improvements, smoother Glass rendering, revamped code blocks and Thinking UI, HTML/PDF chat exports, and new image generation and coding agent features.

Highlights

  • New Qwen3.8-27B Dynamic v3.1 GGUFs.
  • Faster chats: Major performance improvements to streaming, scrolling, menus and dialogs, especially in long conversations.
  • Smoother Glass: Reduced lag while typing, scrolling and generating.
  • Revamped code blocks and Thinking: Independently scrolling, expandable panels with improved syntax highlighting.
  • HTML and PDF exports: Export chats directly from the chat menu.
  • Image queue: Queue upcoming image generations while another is rendering.
  • Claude Code and Codex on MLX: Run coding agents with MLX models through unsloth start.

Chat & UI

  • Streaming performance no longer degrades as conversations grow.
  • Smoother scrolling with background images, with or without Glass.
  • Faster menus, dialogs and browser pane loading.
  • Read aloud starts after the first sentence instead of waiting for the entire response.
  • Chat preferences, time format and spell check now sync with your account.

Images & Video

  • FLUX.2 and FLUX.3 use 36–43% less VRAM during image decoding at the same speed.
  • Queue image generations from the Images page or API.
  • INT8 and FP8 image models now load on older NVIDIA GPUs, including T4.
  • Fixed black image outputs with FLUX.3.
  • LTX-2.5 FP8 now runs on 24 GB GPUs.
  • Cosmos3-Nano can continue video clips from their first or last frames.

Coding Agents & API

  • Run Claude Code and Codex with MLX models on Mac using unsloth start.
  • New Unsloth MCP preset lets coding agents access Unsloth tools.
  • Claude API models without an explicit token limit no longer stop at 1,024 tokens.
  • MLX models now return a proper context-length error instead of an empty response.

Training

  • model.generate() is now 2–8x faster on T4 GPUs by default across FastModel models.
  • Video columns are now correctly supported when training vision models.
  • Ulysses context parallelism now supports Kimi-Linear, DeepSeek, MiniMax and Gemma 4 text models.

entry.title: Large Performance Fixes
entry.content:
This release brings large performance fixes across Unsloth: faster typing and search in long chats, faster image/video loads, two-GPU image/video gen. It also adds separate browsers for each chat, floating browser window.

Highlights

  • Large performance fixes with more Glass theme optimizations coming next week
  • Glass theme fixes no more blur, better rendering, more options
  • Unified memory offloading now properly works for big models
  • Separate browsers for each chat - Multiple chats can now run their own browser individually
  • Floating browser you can move and resize over the chat & let the model do it's thing
  • Dynamic V3.1 Qwen3.8-Flash - 50% less token use, 15% more accurate
  • Two-GPU image and video up to 2x faster on matching NVIDIA cards
  • Faster chat search and deleting - search and delete chats much faster
  • Stable diffusion image/video models loads up to 40% faster
  • LTX-2.5 video much faster for new prompts on 16 to 24 GB GPUs

Chat performance

  • Typing in a long chat no longer lags when a Glass theme or chat background is on.
  • Chat search stays fast on very long histories instead of failing to load.
  • Clearing and deleting chats is much faster on large histories.
  • The first use of voice or audio features after launch no longer freezes a streaming reply for seconds.
  • Read aloud with the Unsloth model engine no longer waits seconds on a model lookup before speaking.
  • Glass themes over a background image respond up to 2x faster without GPU rendering, as on some Linux desktops.

Images and video

  • With two matching, idle NVIDIA GPUs, models such as SDXL, Qwen-Image and Wan2.2 5B run half of each step on the second card when they fit on one, about 1.5 to 1.8x faster.
  • On the same setup, FLUX and Lumina 2 split an even-sized batch of images across both cards.
  • SDXL loads up to 40% faster, so the first image arrives sooner.
  • On 16 to 24 GB GPUs, LTX-2.5 encodes new prompts on the GPU instead of the CPU, so a clip with a new prompt renders much faster.
  • LTX-2.5 GGUF Q8_0 video renders about 10% faster on NVIDIA GPUs, with identical frames.
  • Repeat renders with the same LoRA are faster when the model is not quantized, GGUF or offloaded.
  • Some image models, such as FLUX and Z-Image, render faster on Linux with AMD RDNA3 and RDNA4 GPUs.

New in Unsloth

  • Float the built-in browser over the chat as a small window you can move and resize; each chat remembers whether it floats.
  • Load Anima, Chroma, MOSS-Image and Krea 2 image models from single-file checkpoints, with LoRA and LoKR files for all but Chroma.
  • Glass themes dim the background image instead of blurring it, and controls on other pages match the chat's glass.
  • Owners can rename a managed account without losing its chats, files or settings.
  • Owners can cap model download speed in Settings > General > Downloads.
  • OpenAI-compatible connections can send custom headers.

Fixes

  • On chat-only installs with a non-GGUF model already downloaded, the first chat fetches the default model instead of failing.
  • GGUF models on CPU-only machines no longer run out of memory with Auto context.
  • On Windows, HTTPS downloads resume after a pause or interruption instead of starting over.
  • Updating Unsloth on Windows no longer sits silent for half a minute at the end.
  • Connecting Blender through MCP works again.
  • Compare mode no longer leaves one pane empty on the first message.

Training and library

  • In Python, model.generate() for Llama, Qwen2 and Qwen3 models is faster by default on NVIDIA GPUs under Linux, up to several times for small models.
  • Training on a Hub dataset split into hundreds of files starts up to a minute sooner.
  • With Assistant completions only, answers that start with a newline are no longer left out of training.

Download Unsloth Desktop

Unsloth Desktop is free and open source. Download it for:

Platform Link
Windows Download
macOS Download
Linux x64 / Ubuntu (deb) Download
Linux ARM64 / Ubuntu 24.04+ (deb) Download
Linux x64 (AppImage) Download
Windows ARM64 Download

entry.title: Improved Customization + Glass + Browser Use
entry.content:
This release introduces Qwen3.8-Flash-Next Dynamic V3.1, polishes the Glass themes (now in Beta), adds a Composer position slider and lets models interact with files in the built-in browser. It also brings lower idle memory usage, preserved chat context when switching GGUF models, faster MLX loading and FP8 LoRA training.

Highlights

  • Qwen3.8-Flash-Next Dynamic V3.1 - 10-15% extra accuracy Guide
  • Glass theme improvements across pages, menus, the sidebar and browser
  • Browser file interaction lets models click, read and edit HTML, files and pages
  • Lower idle memory with faster MLX loading and reloading
  • Preserved chat context when switching between GGUF models
  • FP8 LoRA training with lower GPU memory usage
  • Composer position slider to place the chat box anywhere on new chats

Glass and appearance

  • Set the chat box position, from top to bottom, in Settings > Appearance > Composer.
  • Glass themes now have softer highlights, lighter shadows and improved frosted effects across menus, panels and the browser.
  • Pages like Library, Images and Train no longer heavily blur background images.
  • Open conversations now slightly dim the background and use denser glass for the composer.
  • Windows and Linux title bars better match Glass themes and background images.
  • Settings changes made in one browser tab now sync across other open tabs.

Built-in browser

  • With Browser use enabled, models can click and type in HTML and React pages created in chat.
  • Models can read and edit HTML, React, Markdown, code and text files directly in the browser. Back restores the previous version.
  • Models can also read PDFs and other documents open in the browser.
  • Download prompts can remember permissions per site or across all sites, including for program files.

Chat

  • Chats now show activity between tool calls, including context compaction on GGUF models.
  • Attach saved Library files using + > More > Attach from Library.
  • Switching away from a GGUF model and back now preserves chat context, avoiding the need to re-read long histories.
  • GGUF models can read up to four web pages at once when tools run without asking.

Connections and API

  • OpenRouter models now load live, with working Reload models support.
  • Improved compatibility with newer MCP servers.
  • The Decision API adds LiquidAI's d1 models and Decider 2B (MLX only).
  • Settings > API > Quickstart now includes curl, Python and JavaScript examples.

Performance and media

  • Unsloth no longer loads PyTorch and other ML libraries at startup, significantly reducing idle memory usage. Configure startup features in Settings > General > Startup performance.
  • MLX models load and reload much faster, and reducing a loaded model's context now takes seconds.
  • Long prompts on supported MLX models use less memory.
  • SDXL renders faster with very limited VRAM, including 4 GB setups.
  • Image LoRAs in your model folders now appear on the Images page.

Training

  • Faster, lower-memory LoRA training on 16-bit bases with recent NVIDIA GPUs using float8_training = "fp8_lora".
  • DPO, ORPO, KTO, GRPO and CPO training now run on MLX.
  • Fixed crashes when full fine-tuning Gemma 4 in float16.

What's Changed

entry.title: Glass Theme, Personalize & Faster Generation
entry.content:
Unsloth now has Glass themes and more customization options for backgrounds, greetings and chats. This release also brings faster generation, more multi-GPU training options and CPU training in Unsloth.

Highlights

  • New Glass themes with 5 themes, transparency + native macOS glass
  • Customization with custom greetings, background controls and code fonts
  • DeepSeek-V4.1 512K context benchmarks show Unsloth's GGUFs rank strongest across Terminal Bench, DeepSWE and AutomationBench. Analysis
  • Chat navigation to preview, bookmark and jump between earlier turns
  • CPU text training directly from the Train page

Make it yours

  • Choose from five Glass styles with adjustable strength and optional glass menus, with or without a background image.
  • Unsloth Desktop on Mac supports native glass, letting your desktop show through the window.
  • Adjust background size and position, and choose where it appears across your chats.
  • Add your own greeting with text, an icon or an image, or hide it entirely.
  • Customize code fonts, line numbers, word wrapping and ligatures with a live preview.
  • Use the Trick or Treat theme year-round without the seasonal extras.

Chat

  • Preview earlier messages, bookmark turns and jump through long conversations with the new chat navigator.
  • Paste formatted content as Markdown, including links, lists and spreadsheet tables.
  • Arabic, Persian, Hebrew and Urdu messages display right to left while code keeps its original direction.
  • Long chats stay more responsive while replies stream and you scroll.
  • MCP connections recover after a server restart.
  • Coding agents can follow instructions from files in your project's working folder.

Performance and media

  • Supported single-GPU Llama and Qwen3 models generate faster in Unsloth's Transformers backend on NVIDIA GPUs with Linux or WSL. In our A100 test, 4-bit Qwen3-8B reached 99.1 tokens/s, up from 25.7, a 3.9x speedup.
  • SDXL now renders under a 4 GiB VRAM budget, tested on T4 and L4 GPUs.
  • Search large document collections faster with a new index for RAG.
  • Save generated images as PNG faster without changing the output.
  • Video models reuse cached INT8 weights for faster repeat loads.
  • Wan2.2 A14B uses less system memory when building INT8 weights for offloaded generation.
  • Adjust image LoRA strengths without reloading adapter files.
  • Transcribe audio up to four hours long with audio.cpp, subject to upload and storage limits.

Mac

  • Try experimental Fast Verify for faster generation with supported MLX speculative decoding models. Replies may differ slightly.
  • MLX streaming spends less time processing text as replies grow.
  • Unsloth now uses the Mac system font by default.

Training

  • Fine-tune text models on CPU from the Train page when no GPU is available.
  • Chat-only installs can add CPU training through Install Training.
  • Fine-tune audio vision models such as Gemma 3n and Gemma 4 using audio and images together in the same dataset.
  • Load supported non-quantized models larger than a single GPU by loading only each GPU's assigned pipeline layers.
  • Configure supported combinations of data, tensor, pipeline and context parallelism with UNSLOTH_PARALLEL.
  • Reduce MLP activation memory during training with unsloth.tile_mlp(model).
  • Send images to vision models through CLI chat and inference commands.

What's Changed

  • Bump install.sh / install.ps1 pins to unsloth>=2026.10.11 by @danielhanchen in #16131
  • Don't warn about loss_type = "nll" on a TRL whose SFTConfig predates it by @debojyoti-dev in #16042

entry.title: Customize + Performance + UI/UX improvements
entry.content:
Make Unsloth your own with custom backgrounds and a improved UI/UX. This release also cuts app update times and speeds up Linux app and Qwen-Image gen when VRAM is limited. Also new: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 in Unsloth Dynamic v3.1 GGUFs (preview), FLUX.2-klein-9B on low-RAM machines, smoother chats and batched MoE fine-tuning.

Highlights

  • Custom backgrounds to personalize your chats (+ move composer to bottom - more customization coming next week)
  • DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 new Unsloth Dynamic v3.1 GGUFs (preview), the most accurate for their size on nearly all benchmarks Blog
  • 14 new languages for Unsloth
  • App updates finish twice as fast
  • Linux much less lag and improved performance
  • Qwen-Image renders up to 2x faster under a 16 GB VRAM limit
  • Updated interface with consistency and cleaner UI
  • MoE fine-tuning runs compatible API jobs together

Customization and interface

  • Move the chat box to the bottom of new chats with Composer at the bottom in Settings > Chat.
  • Hide the greeting entirely for a simpler new-chat screen.
  • The Library gets shorter chat cards, clearer tooltips and consistent sort and filter icons.
  • Copy images between input slots by dragging a filled slot onto an empty one.
  • Pinned models stay saved across Unsloth Desktop restarts.
  • Each browser tab keeps its own unsent message.
  • Scrolling long chats is smoother on Linux with NVIDIA, X11 and driver 610+. Our high-resolution test improved from about 17 to 60 fps.

Images and video

  • FLUX.2-klein-9B now loads and renders on Linux with 12.7 GB of system RAM and a supported GPU.
  • Qwen-Image-2512 renders up to 2x faster under a 16 GB VRAM limit.
  • Qwen-Image-Edit-2511 renders about 1.3x faster under the same limit.
  • MiniMax-H3 clips finish about 1.7x faster in our memory-limited NVIDIA test.

Performance

  • App updates take about half as long by skipping Python precompilation. The tradeoff is a longer first launch afterwards, as before v0.1.912.
  • Long replies stream more smoothly, even with unfinished math formatting. Parsing an 83 KB reply with a stray $$ took 0.7 seconds instead of 71 seconds.
  • Previewing a 1 GB local Parquet file uses about 300 MB of peak memory, down from 1.5 GB.
  • Unsloth stays responsive as Transformers and MLX models finish loading.

Chat and API

  • GGUF models reload in the background after a llama-server crash.
  • Failed or cancelled GGUF downloads leave your current model loaded.
  • Very long GGUF chats can compact and keep going.
  • Claude Code connected directly to a local GGUF reuses cached prompts across new sessions.
  • Rejected GGUF requests show llama-server’s explanation instead of a generic error.

Mac

  • Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode requests can share an MLX batch. In our test, four simultaneous requests finished up to 2.3x faster.
  • Experimental Neural Engine Prefill processes prompts up to 31% faster in our Qwen3.8-27B-4bit test on M3 Max. It is opt-in and can slightly change replies.
  • Auto context starts GGUF models at no more than 65,536 tokens, reducing upfront memory use. You can still set a larger context manually.
  • Send LFM3-Audio or LFM3-Omni a voice clip on MLX and hear its answer alongside the text.

Training

  • Compatible LoRA and QLoRA jobs on MoE models such as Qwen3.6-35B-A3B train together through the fine-tuning API, each with its own adapter.
  • Use via API on the Train page opens Python, JavaScript and curl examples for your setup.
  • Single-column text datasets are recognised automatically, with no manual column mapping.

What's Changed

  • Bump install.sh / install.ps1 pins to unsloth>=2026.10.10, unsloth-zoo>=2026.10.10 by @danielhanchen in #15785
  • Tensor parallel x FSDP2: average trainable TP parameters left out of FSDP2 over the data parallel ranks by @danielhanchen in #15748
  • Flash impl: warn about an explicit fa3 / fa4 fallback on the Trainer path too by @danielhanchen in #15750
  • FSDP2 block CUDA graphs: free the gathered weights of flex BlockMask blocks by @danielhanchen in #15756
  • Installer downloads: report progress on whole 1 MiB chunks again by @danielhanchen in #15789
  • Studio export: skip the GPU cache clear when nothing was loaded since the last one by @danielhanchen in #15737
  • Studio video: read an LTX-2 checkpoint header once per file when probing for 2.3 by @danielhanchen in #15738
  • Tensor parallel: batch_rebalance and group_by_length samplers give tp peers the same rows by @danielhanchen in #15752
  • CI: hold the unpinned version-compat lanes below torch 2.15 until torchvision 0.30 is published by @danielhanchen in #15774
  • Studio: give each batched fine-tuning job its own fp16 loss scale by @danielhanchen in #15741
  • Studio: list a Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo base pipeline cached in its FP8 mirror On Device by @danielhanchen in #15772

entry.title: Trick or Treat + Optimizations
entry.content:
Halloween 👻 is here. Through October, a Trick or treat row in the sidebar opens eleven Halloween themes, spooky greetings and a few spiders and bats.

This release also speeds up the first launch, Linux tool calls and model loading, and trains compatible fine-tuning jobs together with multi-LoRA.

Highlights

  • Trick or treat: 🎃 new Halloween themes - until Nov 1
  • Faster Unsloth: 2x faster first launch, plus speedups for tool calls, model lists, dataset prep and MiniMax-H3 loads
  • Multi-LoRA batching: up to 4 compatible queued fine-tuning jobs train together
  • SGLang thinking + auto-compact: Resume and JSON output now work on vLLM and SGLang too
  • Browser use switch: let models control the built-in browser from its new tab page

Optimizations

  • Setup now precompiles Python files, so the first launch is about 2x faster.
  • On Linux, tool calls start in 1 to 2 ms instead of 84 to 174 ms with a 2 GB server process.
  • With 497 cached models, the model list uses about a third of the CPU time it did.
  • Preparing a 1,000-row chat dataset for Gemma 3 4B took 1.75 s instead of 6.6 s in our test.
  • MiniMax-H3 loaded in 49 s instead of 61 s on a Linux A100.

Multi-LoRA + API

When several compatible jobs wait in the fine-tuning queue, Unsloth now trains them together, each with its own LoRA adapter on a shared base model.

  • Jobs sent while the GPU is busy queue up in order, and each can be cancelled on its own.
  • Load a job's fine_tuned_model name to chat with its trained adapter.
  • /v1/videos requests now queue while a clip renders, and matching /v1/images/generations requests are batched.

How it works

  • New Triton kernels run the base layer once per batch, while each adapter learns only from its own tokens with its own loss and learning rate.
  • With 4 adapters, a 4096x4096 layer's forward and backward pass ran 1.52x faster than one adapter at a time (A100, bf16, rank 16).

Chat + tools

  • Local models skip tool calls that hit the output limit, so a half-written cat > app.py can't overwrite a file.
  • Before, cut-off rewrites shrank a 175-line test file to as few as 6 lines on an RTX 3090.
  • Thinking models such as Qwen3 and DeepSeek R1 now show their reasoning and the Think toggle on SGLang.
  • With Auto-compact on, long SGLang chats drop their oldest turns and keep answering.
  • On vLLM and SGLang, you can resume a reply cut off at Max Tokens and request JSON with response_format.

Browser + Desktop

  • The browser's new tab page has a Browser use switch that lets models control the browser.
  • On Desktop, a browser agent working for a temporary chat no longer adds pages to your history.
  • On macOS with Safari 18.4 or earlier, Desktop browser tabs and their close buttons work again.
  • Log out is now in the Unsloth Desktop user menu.

Trick or treat

The Trick or treat… row sits above More in the sidebar and opens a Halloween menu.

  • Pick one of eleven themes, such as Pumpkin, Coven and Ghost Ship, each with a light and dark mode.
  • Turn on Spooky greetings and new chats open with a Halloween line and sloth.
  • With Spiders and bats on, Halloween themes get the odd spider and bats crossing the window.
  • Not sure which theme? Trick or treat! picks one at random.

Unsloth returns to normal at midnight on November 1, or right away with Remove now.

Training

  • Gemma 4 E2B and E4B now keep a dataset's thinking text in training instead of dropping it.
  • New chat training setups turn on sequence packing and Assistant completions where the model and data support them.
  • Local JSON and JSONL datasets load even when later rows add new keys.

entry.title: Scheduled + MiniMax-M3.1-Flash + Perf Gains
entry.content:
This release adds scheduled tasks, FLUX-3 edit support, perf improvements and more. Also new: MiniMax-M3.1-Flash, face touch-ups for images and faster performance + chats on Mac.

Highlights

  • Scheduled tasks: Run a prompt on a schedule with a local model or an API
  • MiniMax-M3.1-Flash: MiniMax's 428B MoE (23B active) Guide
  • FLUX 3 Editing: FLUX 3 now supports editing of images with prompts
  • Perf improvements: Large Mac perf gains, less lag, reduced binary sizes
  • Saved presets: Save your Run settings as named presets for each model

Scheduled tasks

  • Open Scheduled from the sidebar's More menu to run a prompt once, daily, on weekdays, weekly or monthly; each answer is saved as a new chat.
  • Each task can run on the loaded model, a model on your device, or a model from a connected API provider.
  • When a task's model isn't loaded, Unsloth asks before loading it, unless you turn on Switch automatically when I'm away.
  • Each task can notify you after every run, only when it fails, or never.
  • Tasks run only while Unsloth is running, without tools or web search.

UI + UX

  • Save Run settings in the model picker as named presets for each model, then rename, delete or switch between them.
  • The preset you picked last is what that model loads with next time, including loads through the API.
  • Chat settings can remember your sampling settings for a model, or reset them to the model's recommended values.
  • GGUF chats now show progress and time left while processing a long prompt, before the reply starts.
  • The API page now shows each served model's context use, speed and request count.
  • Each kind of button and icon now looks the same everywhere in the app.
  • The Library and System pages in Settings show storage as a usage bar, split into models, caches and free space.

Mac

  • MLX chats now reply up to 16% faster with draft models.
  • MLX models that ship with a built-in draft model now use it automatically, with no separate download.
  • Image and video renders need far less memory at the end, so low-memory Macs rarely slow down from swapping.
  • On Apple Silicon, Z-Image GGUFs now make images from text with the MLX engine by default, 1.5-2x faster than before.

Images + video

  • Make videos from text or an image with NVIDIA's Cosmos3-Edge on the Video page.
  • On the Images page, turn on Detailer to redraw faces, hands or other things you name at higher resolution; it needs SAM 3 and a model that can inpaint.
  • On NVIDIA GPUs older than RTX 30-series, Wan2.1 1.3B text-to-video clips render about 5x faster.
  • On NVIDIA GPUs, many image and video models load faster after the first time, since Unsloth saves the version it builds on first load.
  • FLUX.3 Klein can now edit photos in Images > Edit, keeping the photo's dimensions.

Training

  • Split each layer of a model across GPUs for LoRA and QLoRA training, so each GPU holds less: set UNSLOTH_TP_SIZE to the number of GPUs and launch with torchrun.
  • Fine-tuning Unsloth's 4-bit gpt-oss checkpoints no longer crashes on the first training step.
  • GRPO that generates with vLLM runs up to 1.9x faster per step with 16-bit LoRA on Linux with NVIDIA GPUs.
  • GRPO that generates without vLLM runs up to 4.4x faster per step for Llama and Qwen3 on NVIDIA GPUs.

Coding agents + API

  • Apps using an Unsloth API key can no longer approve their own Python or terminal calls to run outside the sandbox.
  • Unsloth no longer trusts forwarded client IPs by default; behind your own reverse proxy, set UNSLOTH_STUDIO_TRUST_FORWARDED=1 or all users share one login rate limit.

Models + hardware

  • Run MiniMax-M3.1-Flash, MiniMax's MoE model for coding, tool use and agent workflows, with up to 1M tokens of context. GGUF
  • At 1-bit, MiniMax-M3.1-Flash needs at least 130 GB of RAM and VRAM combined.
  • On some Windows PCs, GGUF models load again instead of failing every time with "llama-server failed to start".

Download Unsloth Desktop

Unsloth Desktop is free and open source. Download it for:

Platform Link
Windows Download
macOS Download
Linux x64 / Ubuntu (deb) Download
Linux ARM64 / Ubuntu 24.04+ (deb) Download
Linux x64 (AppImage) Download
Windows ARM64 Download

entry.title: MOSS-Image, Flint & NVIDIA Bolt E4B
entry.content:
Recursive's Flint, MOSS-Image and NVIDIA's Nemotron Bolt 4B are here! Run them locally in Unsloth. Also new: a chat-only Unsloth Desktop install, MLX MoE models bigger than your Mac's memory and an OpenAI-compatible fine-tuning API.

Highlights

  • Bigger MoE models on Mac: MLX MoE models too big for memory keep experts on SSD, so Qwen3.8-Flash-Next runs on a 32 GB Mac.
  • Chat-only install: a much smaller Unsloth Desktop for GGUF chat; add training later in Settings.
  • Flint: Recursive's 40B coding-agent MoE, runs in 24 GB at 3-bit Guide
  • MOSS-Image: 5.1B image model designed for top-tier generation GGUF + FP8
  • NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B: NVIDIA's new Gemma 4 E4B fine-tune, 63.2 on Tau2-Bench vs the original's 38.7 Guide
  • MoE expert pruning: Export a smaller MoE model by removing 25% or 50% of its least useful experts with REAP.
  • UI overhaul: New + more consistent UI across Unsloth (API, roundness etc)

Images + video

  • Generate images containing English or Chinese text with OpenMOSS's 5.1B MOSS-Image, SFT or Base. GGUF · Base GGUF
  • MOSS-Image, the new image model, runs on 16 GB GPUs; its GGUFs also run on Macs and computers without a supported GPU.
  • Most image and video models too big for one GPU now split across your NVIDIA GPUs, if they fit, instead of streaming from system memory.
  • The new Hires fix upscales and refines a render in one step on SDXL, FLUX.1, Qwen-Image and Z-Image.
  • The new Compare grid renders one prompt while varying up to three settings, such as seed, CFG or LoRA weight, in labelled grids.
  • SDXL safetensors get AUTOMATIC1111-style prompt weighting, CLIP skip, CFG rescale, variation seeds and textual inversion.
  • Pasted AUTOMATIC1111, Forge or Civitai parameter blocks fill in the Images page settings.
  • If SAM 3 isn't already downloaded, the Mask from text tool now uses SAM 3.1: smaller, with no Hugging Face login.

Chat + Desktop

  • Pick Chat only (GGUF) when first launching Unsloth Desktop for a much smaller install; add training later in Settings.
  • Settings > Chat now lets you view, edit, clear or turn off the memory notes Unsloth sends to every chat.
  • In document-search chats, Show passages lists the exact text the model got and opens each passage at its page.
  • The Audio page can speak and transcribe via a saved API connection, such as OpenAI or a local server.
  • Unsloth installs, updates and pip install -U unsloth now reject eMudhra's compromised emSign certificates, which let attackers impersonate websites. The optional vLLM and SGLang engines still trust them.

Flint

  • Run Recursive's Flint, a 40B MoE model with 2.5B active parameters for coding agents, with reasoning, tool use and 256K context. Guide · GGUF
  • At 3-bit, Flint fits in 24 GB at short contexts.
  • On SWE-bench Pro v2, Flint scores 89.7 vs Qwen 3.6's 73.8.

NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B

  • Run and fine-tune NVIDIA's Gemma Nemotron 4B, a Gemma 4 E4B reasoning tune for tool calling and instruction following.
  • Gemma Nemotron 4B beats Gemma 4 E4B on 16 of 21 NVIDIA tests, gaining most in tool use and multi-turn chat.
  • DPO on Gemma 4 E2B and E4B, including Gemma Nemotron 4B, no longer crashes.

Training

  • Fine-tuning Whisper, Canary, Moonshine, Dia and CTC speech models with FastModel no longer fails.
  • Parakeet, Canary and CTC speech training uses up to 55% less memory.
  • The new Books & Documents to Text recipe in Data Recipes turns ebooks and documents into a pretraining text dataset, no model needed.
  • On Windows and Linux, the Export page can now prune 25% or 50% of a MoE model's least useful experts with REAP, at some quality cost.
  • In Python, reap_prune runs REAP expert pruning up to 54x faster than llm-compressor's.
  • unsloth train now trains vision and, except on Mac, audio models.
  • Unsloth now supports OpenAI's fine-tuning API, so OpenAI's SDK can upload datasets and run supervised fine-tuning of local models.

Performance

  • MLX MoE models too big for your Mac keep experts on SSD, with slower replies. Qwen3.8-Flash-Next fits a 32 GB Mac; DeepSeek-V4-Flash and GLM-5.3-Flash need far less memory than their size.
  • DPO and other training that pads sequences runs up to 3.8x faster with less memory on NVIDIA Ampere or newer.
  • Qwen3-MoE, Gemma 3 and Gemma 4 training on GPUs without bf16 now uses up to 7x less attention memory with torch 2.13 or older.

Coding agents + API

  • In chat, models can now read text files and documents on connected MCP servers, not just use their tools.
  • When launching coding agents, unsloth start no longer sends its Unsloth API key in plain text through your HTTP proxy to a local Unsloth.
  • On Windows, unsloth start no longer breaks Claude Code hooks or Codex sign-in when launching them.
  • Requests with an Unsloth API key can no longer run Python and terminal tools unsandboxed; only the Unsloth UI can allow that.
  • The new Save for this model button in Chat settings makes your sampling settings that model's default for new chats and API requests.

Models + hardware

  • A BF16 gpt-oss checkpoint loaded with load_in_4bit = True no longer gets random expert and router weights.
  • The model picker again lets you run models on Ryzen AI 300-series and newer NPUs, with no environment variable.
  • On some Linux AMD PCs with a system-wide ROCm, GGUFs that ran on the CPU now run on the GPU again.

Download Unsloth Desktop

Unsloth Desktop is free and open source. Download it for:

Platform Link
Windows Download
macOS Download
Linux x64 / Ubuntu (deb) Download
Linux ARM64 / Ubuntu 24.04+ (deb) Download
Linux x64 (AppImage) Download
Windows ARM64 Download

entry.title: DeepSeek-V4.1 & FLUX-3
entry.content:
DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 and FLUX.3 Image Klein are here! Run both locally in Unsloth. Also new: images and videos in chat, multi-GPU training with FSDP2 (alpha) and one-command MCP setup for coding agents.

Highlights

  • DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017: 552B (16B active) - runs on ~125 GB at 1-bit with its Engram table on SSD Guide
  • FLUX.3 Image Klein: Runs on 24 GB and edits with up to 10 reference images GGUF
  • One-command MCP setup: unsloth mcp add connects Claude Code, Codex or Cursor to Unsloth.
  • Images and videos in chat: Local chat models use the image or video model loaded beside them.
  • Qwen-Image-Edit-2509 and 2511: Edit with up to 3 images at once.
  • Token preview: See what your model will learn before training starts.

DeepSeek-V4.1

  • Run DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017, an update to DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with better reasoning, coding and agentic results, and shorter outputs. It has 552B parameters plus 196B in its Engram table, about 16B active, and 1M tokens of context. With the Engram table left on SSD, it runs in about 125 GB of memory at 1-bit, or 300 GB at 4-bit. Guide · GGUF
  • DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 scores 42.3 on Terminal-Bench 4.0, up from 31.2 for the earlier DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash.
  • Thinking is on by default at high effort. Choose any effort from low to max, or turn thinking off.

FLUX.3 Image Klein

  • Generate and edit images with Black Forest Labs' FLUX.3 Image Klein, a 5.6B model that renders text and edits with up to 10 reference images. It runs on 24 GB of GPU memory, its GGUFs also run on computers without a supported GPU, and the undistilled Klein Base is available too. GGUF · Base GGUF
  • Enhance prompt, on by default, expands short prompts into detailed captions, which fixes most distorted bodies in hard poses. Preview shows the caption so you can copy or edit it.

Images + video

  • Qwen-Image-Edit-2509 and Qwen-Image-Edit-2511 now accept up to 3 images per edit.
  • Set custom video sizes and aspect ratios in Create videos, or pick one of the model's trained sizes.
  • Start an edit straight from an image's menu in the Images gallery or the Library, or drag a generated image onto an image picker on the Images page.
  • Image and video models with a large text encoder now load a quantized encoder by default where the GPU supports it, cutting the encoder's memory by up to half and loading faster. LTX-2.5 no longer needs a Hugging Face login.

Chat + Desktop

  • Image, video and Read aloud speech models can now stay loaded beside your chat model on computers with a dedicated GPU. Pick When they fit or Always in Settings > Resources > Model memory.
  • With the Images pill on, a local chat model can use the image or video model loaded beside it to make images and playable videos in the chat.
  • After an image or video model replaces your GGUF chat model, the chat continues without re-reading the conversation, as long as Keep chat context across unloads is on.
  • In Unsloth Desktop, choose an existing working folder when creating a project.
  • Unsloth Desktop no longer crashes at startup on older macOS versions, and its browser panel works on macOS 27 and follows system proxies such as Clash.

Training

  • In Python, spread LoRA, QLoRA and full fine-tuning across GPUs with FSDP2, and split long sequences, including packed ones, with context_parallel_size. Check the machine first with unsloth doctor --gpus.
  • On the Train page, Preview tokens shows which parts of your dataset the model trains on and flags samples cut off by the context limit. Data Recipe chats now train as multi-turn conversations, and Qwen fine-tunes keep a dataset's thinking text.
  • Cut full fine-tuning optimizer memory with optim = "adamw_flash", or set UNSLOTH_OFFLOAD_OPTIMIZER_STATE=1 to keep optimizer state in system memory between steps at some cost in speed.

Performance

  • Local GGUF chats with tools now show replies as fast as the model writes them, so the next tool call no longer waits, and long replies no longer slow down as they grow.
  • LoRA training with lora_dropout or lora_bias now runs on Unsloth's fused kernels, about 28% faster per step.
  • Gemma 4's global attention layers train on a new kernel on NVIDIA Ampere or newer GPUs, with 1.4x to 2.1x faster attention and up to 4.9x less attention memory.
  • Qwen3.8-Flash-Next on MLX is up to 1.4x faster on M5 Macs and up to 1.2x faster on M1 to M4 Macs.
  • On M1 to M4 Macs, 4-bit and 8-bit MLX models generate several chats at once up to 1.8x faster.

Coding agents

  • Connect Claude Code, Codex or Cursor to Unsloth's MCP server with unsloth mcp add claude-code (or codex, cursor).
  • Agents can upload datasets, start training and load the resulting checkpoint.
  • Agents can also download models ahead of time, preview what a model load will download or unload, and queue video generation jobs.

Models + settings

  • Filter downloaded models by capability or format, including Exports & Fine-tunes, and search for a maker such as DeepSeek or Meta to list Unsloth's uploads of its models.
  • QwenCloud and Z.ai are now available as API providers.
  • Export token usage from Profile stats as CSV.
  • unsloth run passes llama-server short flags such as -ctv, -dev and -ctxcp through unchanged.

Hardware compatibility

  • PCs without an NVIDIA GPU or ROCm, such as Snapdragon laptops and Linux ARM boards, now run GGUFs on their GPU through Vulkan instead of the CPU.
  • NVIDIA MIG slices are sized and selected correctly, and machines that mix GPU generations get settings and llama.cpp builds every GPU can run.
  • On Linux machines with an AMD Strix APU and a discrete AMD GPU, PyTorch is installed for the discrete GPU. On Windows AMD PCs with the HIP SDK, Settings > System no longer asks for administrator access.
  • Windows on ARM PCs can now turn on Sandbox High in Settings > Sandbox.

Download Unsloth Desktop

Unsloth Desktop is free and open source. Download it for:

Platform Link
Windows Download
macOS Download
Linux x64 / Ubuntu (deb) Download
Linux ARM64 / Ubuntu 24.04+ (deb) Download
Linux x64 (AppImage) Download
Windows ARM64 Download

What's Changed

  • Bump install.sh / install.ps1 pins to unsloth>=2026.10.6, unsloth-zoo>=2026.10.6 by @danielhanchen in #13918
  • Studio: preview tokens and the completion mask before training by @danielhanchen in #13850
  • Locate the MTP drafter-drop fallback by its shape, not one spelling by @danielhanchen in #13922
  • Fix main's red Backend CI after #13850 and #13806 by @danielhanchen in #13930
  • Studio: do not re-send the image generate POST after a dropped connection by @drakeo338 in #13790
  • NVFP4: decode weight tiles inside the GEMM for small-batch forward and dX by @danielhanchen in #13840

entry.title: Meta Muse Spark Open + NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5
entry.content:
Run NVIDIA's new Nemotron 3.5 models and Meta's new Muse Spark Open locally in Unsloth. New: text-diffusion LLMs, DeepSpeed training and better prompt caching for coding agents.

Highlights

  • NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Bolt: Run on 24 GB of memory. Guide
  • NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super VL: 120B (12B active) Guide
  • Meta Muse Spark Open: 816B (42.7B active) - runs on 256GB Guide
  • Better prompt caching for coding agents: Claude Code, Codex etc. on local GGUF models re-process far less of each prompt.
  • Browser use: Always allow properly works, cursor, and separate tabs for each chat.
  • Images through your connections: generate with sd-server, Ollama, Lemonade and other image servers.
  • Diffusion LLMs: train and chat with LLaDA, Dream, SDAR and more, with a live denoising canvas.

Nemotron 3.5

  • Run NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super VL, a 120B model with 12B active parameters and up to 1M tokens of context, built for document understanding, computer use and long-running agents. Super VL runs in about 64 GB of memory at 1-bit, or 128 GB at 4-bit. Guide · GGUF
  • Run NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Bolt, a 74B model with 9B active parameters and 128K context, compressed from Super VL. Bolt runs in about 32 GB of memory at 1-bit or 2-bit. Guide · GGUF
  • Nemotron 3.5 Super VL generates about 5x faster than Inkling Small at 100K input with similar intelligence.
  • By default, Unsloth runs Nemotron 3.5 Bolt with a DSpark drafter (about 1 to 2 GB more memory) and Super VL with its built-in MTP for faster output. Both can be turned off in settings. MTP Guide

Muse Spark Open

  • Run Meta's Muse Spark Open, an 816B MoE model with about 42.7B active parameters and 1M tokens of context, built for multimodal reasoning, coding and agentic workflows. Muse Spark Open runs in about 256 GB of memory at 2-bit. Guide · GGUF
  • Muse Spark Open takes text, images, video and audio as input, with reasoning effort from low to xhigh.
  • Muse Spark Open was trained on long-horizon coding tasks, including whole-repository generation, large end-to-end projects and auto-research.

Training

  • Train and chat with text-diffusion LLMs in the Unsloth app, including LLaDA, Dream, SDAR, LLaDA2, Nemotron-Labs-Diffusion and DiffusionGemma. Chat replies show a live denoising canvas.
  • Train with DeepSpeed ZeRO-2 and ZeRO-3, including 4-bit QLoRA, full fine-tuning, DPO and CPU offload. LoRA training with DDP and gradient checkpointing also no longer crashes.
  • GRPO with fast_inference now runs on Nemotron 3 Nano and block-FP8 MoE models, sharing weights with vLLM.
  • On the Train page, stop early when eval loss stops improving and train on pre-tokenized datasets. Random Seed now also sets the LoRA starting weights.

Performance

  • When Claude Code, Codex or OpenCode runs on a local GGUF model, follow-up turns re-process much less of the conversation, and a new Claude Code session's first reply starts up to 4x sooner.
  • In Python, single-prompt model.generate is up to 2.7x faster at 32K context for Llama and Qwen3 models.
  • In Python, generating 2 to 4 prompts at once with a bitsandbytes 4-bit model is up to 2.8x faster on some NVIDIA GPUs.
  • GRPO rollouts with fast_inference on Nemotron 3 Nano are up to 30% faster by default.

Browser use

  • See a cursor where the model clicks and types, or turn it off in Settings > Browser > Browser use > Show cursor.
  • Browser use prompts now have Always allow, which approves that kind of action on a site for the rest of the chat. Scripts still ask every time.
  • Each chat keeps its own browser tabs, and in Desktop, browser use keeps working in chats that are not on screen.
  • In the web UI, browser pages remember site preferences between pages, load data from their own site, and play videos full screen.

Images + video

  • Generate images on the Images page through a connected image server, such as sd-server, Ollama, Lemonade, vLLM, llama.cpp or a custom OpenAI-compatible URL.
  • Image and video models now skip text-encoder layers they never use, saving memory on every load.

Chat + Desktop

  • Choose where Unsloth installs on Windows from Desktop's first-run screen.
  • Re-embed your documents after switching the embedding model, without uploading them again.
  • Chat with files can collapse to a row of pills, its citations open a PDF at the cited page, and newly added Word and HTML files keep their list numbers.
  • Compact a conversation from the chat header menu, and Rewind no longer asks for confirmation when no files changed.

Models + settings

  • When Claude Code, OpenCode or Codex runs on a cloud model, add --auto-route to unsloth start to send routine coding work, such as reading files, searching and running commands, to your local model.
  • Codex can use its MCP and sub-agent tools with local models, and Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode can run on a model from Settings > Connections with unsloth start --model.
  • Name a model once in Settings > API > Model aliases, so apps using the Unsloth API keep working when the model behind the alias changes.
  • vLLM connections and Unsloth's own vLLM engine support thinking effort levels and Preserve thinking, and the engine now auto-compacts long chats. vLLM and SGLang loads can also set an FP8 KV cache, a GPU memory limit and a seed.
  • Pick 2-bit, 4-bit, 6-bit or 8-bit from MLX repos that publish several precisions, the way you pick GGUF quants. Xing4.0 and MiniCPM-V 4.7 now run and train with MLX.

Hardware compatibility

  • Windows PCs with NVIDIA drivers older than CUDA 12 install the Vulkan or CPU llama.cpp build instead of failing.
  • AMD GPUs that ROCm does not support, such as RDNA 1 and Polaris, now get the Vulkan llama.cpp build even when ROCm is installed or another AMD GPU supports it.
  • GGUF image generation runs on Vulkan for AMD and Intel Arc GPUs when PyTorch is CPU-only.
  • Windows installs on PyTorch 2.10 and 2.11 get prebuilt flash-attn, causal-conv1d and mamba-ssm.
  • Multi-GPU machines that mix GPU generations now pick the attention backend for each GPU, and Hopper GPUs with conda-forge xformers no longer crash.

Download Unsloth Desktop

Unsloth Desktop is free and open source. Download it for:

Platform Link
Windows Download
macOS Download

Linux x64 (AppImage) Download
